lines.text: Have you ever noticed how highway exit numbers skip from Exit twelve straight to Exit twenty-five?
It is not because the department of transportation forgot how to count.
In the United States, most interstate highway exit numbers correspond directly to mile markers, not exit counts.
Exit twenty-five means you are exactly twenty-five miles away from the state border or highway beginning.
This mile-post system allows drivers to instantly calculate how many miles remain until their turn.
It also lets road engineers build brand new exits between existing ones without renumbering hundreds of signs.
The mile-marker system turns every highway into a giant built-in odometer for road trippers.
